column1: #   Maps AOP-Wiki key events of the respiratory AOP network (Aop:148, 411,
#   424, 425) to Reactome pathways, as candidate key-event-equivalents or
#   causally neighboring mechanisms. Candidates were generated from each
#   key event's grounded composition: protein object terms joined to
#   Reactome via PR -> UniProt cross-reference, process terms matched by
#   lexical search of the Reactome pathway index; all against Reactome
#   release 98 (ContentService, queried 2026-11-09), every stable id and
#   label re-verified against the live service on the mapping_date. Most
#   predicates are deliberately weaker than exactMatch: a Reactome pathway
#   is often causally adjacent to a key event (e.g. cilium assembly vs
#   beat frequency) rather than equivalent to it. Rows with object_id
#   sssom:NoTermFound are negative receipts per docs/grounding-receipts.md
#   class 5: Reactome was searched and holds no human pathway for that key
#   event, typically because it sits above the cellular level of
#   biological organization. All rows are agent-proposed and await curator

column10: The key event is the receptor activation that initiates this pathway, not the pathway itself. Via PR:000006933 -> UniProt:P00533 cross-reference to Reactome v98. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

column2: Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Regulator Function, Decreased
column10: This disease pathway models exactly the decreased-CFTR-function state the key event asserts. CFTR (UniProt:P13569) was inferred from the key event title because the event has no object term component - a class-4 curator-judgment receipt; confirmation required. Reactome v98. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

column2: Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Regulator Function, Decreased
column10: Trafficking regulation of the channel whose function the key event asserts decreased; a mechanism that can produce the key event, not the event itself. CFTR (UniProt:P13569) inferred from the key event title (no object term component); class-4 receipt, confirmation required. Reactome v98. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

Assembly of the motile cilium is causally upstream of its beating function; the key event concerns the function, which Reactome does not model directly. Lexical search of Reactome v98 pathway index. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.
Parent assembly pathway (covers primary as well as motile cilia); weaker fit than R-HSA-9975924. Lexical search of Reactome v98 pathway index. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

FOXJ1 is the master regulator this pathway is organized around and its only Reactome pathway; the key event (decreased FOXJ1 protein) is a perturbed state of this program rather than strictly identical to it, hence closeMatch not exactMatch. Via PR:000007628 -> UniProt:Q92949 cross-reference to Reactome v98. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

Motile cilia number and length are the direct outcome of 9+2 motile cilium assembly, the process this pathway models. Lexical search of Reactome v98 pathway index. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.

Intraflagellar transport builds and maintains ciliary length; a sub-mechanism of the change the key event describes. Lexical search of Reactome v98 pathway index. Agent-proposed, pending curator confirmation.
